final_answer:
BOARD MEMORANDUM - PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL (draft for GC review; outside counsel review required before distribution per Monitoring Manual s.7)
TO: Board of Directors, Greenleaf Industries, Inc. | FROM: Marcus Chen, In-House Regulatory Counsel, through Diana Whitmore, GC | RE: SEC 2023 beneficial ownership amendments and Greenleaf's shareholder situation | Facts as of late February 2025.

1. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
- The SEC's amendments (Rel. No. 34-98704, Oct. 10, 2023) shortened Schedule 13D/13G deadlines (effective Sept. 30, 2024) and required structured XML filing (Dec. 18, 2024). Investors now disclose faster, so we get less warning-free time but also less time to respond.
- Thornfield's Schedule 13D was TIMELY. Investor Relations' "one day late" count is wrong because it counted Monday, Jan. 20, 2025 (Martin Luther King Jr. Day, a federal holiday). Five business days from the Tuesday, Jan. 14 crossing: Jan. 15, 16, 17, 21, 22. The Jan. 22 filing was the fifth. We should not raise lateness with anyone.
- The advance-notice window dates in our materials appear to be miscomputed by one day. The bylaw (as summarized by IR; the bylaw text was not in my file) runs from the anniversary of last year's meeting (June 12, 2024), giving Feb. 12 to Mar. 14, 2025, not Feb. 11 to Mar. 13. Either way, the window closes before the Mar. 18 board meeting. Recommendation: interim board contact before Mar. 13.
- Thornfield's true economic exposure is higher than the 5.46% on its cover page: it holds cash-settled swaps on 2.3 million shares (1.24%). Direct plus swap exposure is 12.4 million shares (6.70%).
- No group is established on present facts; the evidence is circumstantial. A Thornfield-Ridgeview group would hold 9.26% directly (10.50% counting swaps), below our 15% rights-plan trigger.
- The Apex dinner is unconfirmed intelligence and should be treated as a risk factor only.
- Our VantagePoint monitoring has material gaps and the Monitoring Manual is out of date.

2. WHAT CHANGED (verified against the Adopting Release as described by multiple law-firm summaries; the primary SEC text could not be fetched in this environment, so rule-text cites should be confirmed on eCFR before distribution)
a) Schedule 13D: initial filing within 5 business days (was 10 calendar days). Amendments for material changes within 2 business days (was "promptly"). A 1% change in holdings is deemed material. Our November 2023 Stonebridge bulletin says amendments remain "promptly"; that is incorrect, and the Feb. 20, 2025 Stonebridge letter correctly states 2 business days.
b) Schedule 13G: passive investors (Rule 13d-1(c)): initial within 5 business days; qualified institutional investors ("QIIs", Rule 13d-1(b)) and exempt investors: initial within 45 days after the end of the calendar quarter in which 5% is crossed. Amendments for material changes: 45 days after quarter-end (quarterly, was annual). Ten-percent and 5-point-change amendments: passive investors within 2 business days; QIIs/exempt investors within 5 business days after the end of the MONTH in which the threshold is crossed. The bulletin, the Feb. 20 letter and our Manual say QIIs file within 5 business days of crossing 10%; secondary sources indicate the month-end trigger. Confirm against Rule 13d-2(d). Note that "QIB" in our documents should read "QII"; "QIB" is a different 144A concept.
c) Group formation: the SEC did not adopt its proposed "tipper-tippee" rule and did not adopt new rule-text safe harbors. It issued guidance that (i) a group requires some agreement, arrangement, understanding or concerted action, though not necessarily express; and (ii) an independent, free exchange of ideas among shareholders, without more, does not form a group. It amended Rule 13d-5(b) so acquisitions by group members are imputed to the group. The bulletin overstates this as a codified safe harbor, and the Feb. 20 letter and Manual overstate the rule as "expanded" group formation. The board should understand the real change is modest: the test remains facts-and-circumstances, and parallel trading plus a shared solicitor is not itself a group.
d) Cash-settled derivatives: the SEC did not adopt the proposed rule deeming such holders beneficial owners; it issued guidance (extending its security-based-swap guidance) that facts such as purpose or effect of influencing control, counterparty hedging, and parallel direct holdings are relevant. The bulletin and letter describe this as "amendments to Rule 13d-3"; I treat it as guidance, which makes it uncertain and fact-dependent. Rule 13d-3(d)(1) (right to acquire within 60 days) is the separate hook if a swap allows physical settlement.
e) 13G-to-13D conversion: a filer that loses 13G eligibility must now file a 13D within 5 business days (was 10 days), per Rules 13d-1(e)-(g). The bulletin and the Feb. 20 letter state "10 calendar days" and call the cooling-off new; both are wrong on the filing deadline. The prohibition on voting and acquiring existed previously and runs from the loss of eligibility until 10 days after the 13D is filed (my recollection of Rule 13d-1(e)(2); confirm).
f) XML: all 13D/13G filings from Dec. 18, 2024 must use a custom XML schema (not inline XBRL). Apex's Feb. 12, 2025 13G/A: XML compliance not yet checked. Its timing is fine: 45 days after Dec. 31, 2024 is Feb. 14.
g) Also relevant and post-dating the bulletin: on Feb. 11, 2025 SEC staff revised Reg. 13D-G C&DI 103.11 and added 103.12 stating that pressuring management (as opposed to discussing views) on matters such as board changes or business divestitures may disqualify an investor from 13G. Neither Stonebridge document mentions it. It directly bears on Apex.

3. APPLICATION TO OUR HOLDERS
Thornfield (10.1M sh, 5.46%; Rule 13d-1(a)): Filing timely as above. Items to flag: (1) The cover page excerpt shows Row 2 (group box) unchecked and Item 6 says Row 12 is checked, but the excerpt does not show a mark; read the EDGAR original. (2) Item 6 discloses swaps but excludes them from 5.5%; the swaps expire June-Dec. 2025. The exclusion is defensible on the face of the filing (cash-settled only, no right to vote or acquire) but we cannot rule out a purpose-or-effect argument given its activist posture, direct holdings, and possible counterparty hedging; it is a contestable position, not a violation. (3) IR says Thornfield bought another 400,000-600,000 shares in February, which would put it at about 10.5-10.7M (5.7-5.8%), yet IR's table still uses 10.1M. Those purchases alone (under 1% of the class) may not require a 13D/A, but Item 4 changes (e.g., a nomination, Ridgeview coordination) would require an amendment within 2 business days. Watch for it. (4) IR's memo is dated Feb. 26 but reports data "as of Feb. 28"; its figures are estimates.
Ridgeview (7.03M, 3.80%): below 5%, no filing duty alone. Coordination evidence (simultaneous buying, shared Copperfield, similar analyst questions) is circumstantial and sourced to a vendor algorithm that the Manual admits produces false positives and to informal contacts; a shared solicitor and same-thesis investing are not an agreement. If a group exists, members would aggregate to 17.13M (9.26%) and would owe a group 13D within 5 business days of the group's acquiring more than 5%; Thornfield's Item 2 box and Item 6 denial of other arrangements would then be inaccurate, a basis for demanding correction. Note Thornfield's 13D states no other arrangements exist; if untrue, that is a disclosure claim. Recommendation: no accusation now; build a record (Item 5 transactions, solicitor engagement letters, nomination notice contents, which often reveal joint proposals).
Apex (15.17M, 8.20%, QII on 13G): the Feb. 5 dinner is single-sourced hearsay; Ms. Whitmore directs it be framed as a risk. Under the guidance, attending a discussion with activists, without more, does not defeat 13G eligibility or form a group. Risk arises if Apex pressures management, agrees to vote with Thornfield, or otherwise acts to influence control. If so, Apex must file a 13D within 5 business days and may not vote or buy until 10 days after filing; Apex's 8.2% would be sidelined, which matters for a contest. We have no right to demand certification; any inquiry should be careful, counsel-led, and avoid selective-disclosure or Regulation FD problems.

4. MONITORING ADEQUACY (VantagePoint and Manual)
Gaps: (1) no cash-settled swap or OTC data, so Thornfield's 2.3M shares are invisible to alerts; (2) alerts are keyed to direct holdings only and could miss a group crossing 15% with swaps counted; (3) Manual still states 10-day 13D and annual 13G rules in places, says QIIs file "promptly" at 10%, and has no quarterly-amendment calendar, 2-business-day 13D/A tracking, or business-day counter that handles federal holidays (the very error IR made); (4) vendor XML parsing was only promised; confirm it works; (5) weekly transfer-agent data; (6) correlation algorithm yields false positives. Also the Manual's internal review times conflict (24 hours versus one business day; 48-hour analysis). Fix: update Manual now, add holiday-aware calendar, obtain swap/13D Item 6 tracking, run NOBO/OBO pull, and add 13D/A watch.

5. DEFENSIVE CONSIDERATIONS
Advance notice: see above. Confirm exact bylaw text (anniversary versus meeting date; notice contents; whether a meeting-date change of more than 30 days resets the window) with Stonebridge. Under Rule 14a-19 (universal proxy; from my recollection, not re-verified), a dissident's nominee notice is due 60 days before the anniversary, about Apr. 13, 2025, so a contest could still be launched after the bylaw window if the bylaw is not enforced strictly; evaluate the bylaw's validity and enforceability under governing state law (state of incorporation is not in my file; if Delaware, advance-notice bylaws are reviewed for equitable reasons, and recent Delaware decisions such as Kellner v. AIM ImmunoTech (Del. 2024) tightened scrutiny of board-adopted bylaws; I have not independently verified these authorities).
Rights plan (15% trigger; shelf; 185M shares so 27.75M shares): Thornfield + Ridgeview 17.13M (9.26%), gap 10.62M shares (5.74 points). If swaps are counted by the plan's definition, 19.43M (10.50%), gap 8.32M. If Apex were somehow added, 32.30M (17.46%), over the trigger; Apex plus Thornfield alone is 25.27M (13.66%). All need the plan text (not provided) to confirm whether derivatives and "acting in concert" count. Activating now against a stake of roughly 9% with no confirmed group, no public campaign and no nomination would face enhanced scrutiny under Delaware law (Unocal; Moran v. Household; Air Products v. Airgas; Williams Cos. S'holder Litig. (Del. Ch. 2021) invalidating a low-threshold, broadly worded pill) - cited from general knowledge, not verified here. A reactive pill with a lowered trigger and a wide group/derivative definition is the most litigation-exposed form. Recommendation: do not activate or lower the trigger at March 18 absent new facts; refresh the plan, brief the board on a fiduciary record, and be ready to act on a trigger event (a nomination plus confirmed group, or accumulation toward 12-13%).

6. RECOMMENDATIONS (priority order)
1. Before Mar. 13: Ms. Whitmore briefs the board chair/lead director; hold a short telephonic session; pre-clear a nomination-response protocol with Stonebridge.
2. Confirm bylaw window math and notice requirements; treat Mar. 13 as the working deadline and Mar. 14 as the likely legal one.
3. Correct the record: do not assert Thornfield filed late; correct IR's memo.
4. Ask Stonebridge to correct and update its bulletin and Feb. 20 letter (13D/A 2-day rule, 13D conversion deadline, QII month-end 10% rule, derivatives and group as guidance, Feb. 11, 2025 C&DIs). The Feb. 20 letter itself says it is not exhaustive and does not account for later SEC guidance.
5. Monitor Thornfield for 13D/A within 2 business days of any material change or group; check Item 5 and exhibit C.
6. Evaluate swap-beneficial-ownership position only after reviewing Exhibit C; consider reserving rights, not threatening.
7. Treat Apex as a watch item; no outreach beyond ordinary engagement without counsel.
8. Update Monitoring Manual, VantagePoint (swaps, XML, quarterly 13G), and pull a NOBO/OBO list.
9. Pill: shelf status maintained; review plan definitions; board education session.

Note: figures use 185,000,000 shares; Ridgeview and Apex numbers are IR estimates/13G/A-based. Ms. Whitmore asked that this be done in-house; the above flags where outside-counsel confirmation of rule text and state law remains advisable.
